description:
Split out of op-375p / gh:#41, where it was only a comment. Concrete work with a clear verification, not scoping. gh:#42 https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/42

THE PROBLEM. CE Monte Carlo cannot run inside a coupled transient, so pebble-bed and MSR multiphysics needs collapsed multigroup constants a diffusion/SP3/SN solver can march. This workspace has both ends of that chain and none of the middle.

SURVEYED 2026-09-04, three findings.

  1. NO GENERATION PATH. outram_mc_libs::physics::physics_mg defines Mgxs and MgxsLibrary and run_keff_mg consumes them, but Mgxs::new has NO call site anywhere outside its own definition. Every multigroup library must currently be typed in by hand. The MC can use group constants and cannot produce them.
  2. NO MGXS TALLIES. Generation needs flux and reaction-rate tallies binned by energy group and by zone/material, plus a group-to-group scatter matrix. None of those scores exist.
  3. TWO INCOMPATIBLE TYPES, no converter. outram_mc_libs::Mgxs is transport-flavoured (total, scatter matrix, nu-fission, chi). genfoam::xs::GroupConstants is diffusion-flavoured (diffusion_coefficient in m, nu_sigma_f, sigma_pow = kappa-Sigma_f in J/m, sigma_removal, chi_prompt, chi_delayed).

Three steps then, and the third carries real physics: D = 1/(3 Sigma_tr), removal = absorption + out-scatter, and a prompt/delayed chi split needing delayed-neutron data the transport-side Mgxs does not carry.

THE DETAIL THAT DECIDES THE DESIGN. genfoam::xs::NuclearDataOneEnergy already exposes get(parameters, is_parametrize) with a poly_spline_mode — genfoam ALREADY supports cross sections parametrised on state. So the deliverable is not one library at one state point but XS tables over state: temperature, density, and for a pebble bed burnup. That is what multiphysics needs, because Doppler feedback is the whole point of a coupled transient and a single-state library cannot express it. The consumer anticipated this; the producer does not exist.

SCOPE.
  1. MGXS tallies in outram-mc-libs — flux, absorption, nu-fission, kappa-fission, group-to-group scatter matrix, binned by group and by zone/material. LOAD-BEARING; the rest is arithmetic.
  2. Flux-weighted collapse to Mgxs, gated on the existing Mgxs::consistency_residual.
  3. Bridge Mgxs -> GroupConstants. DOCUMENT the diffusion-coefficient convention chosen (transport-corrected vs out-scatter) — silently picking one is how a deterministic solution quietly disagrees with its own MC reference.
  4. Parametrised libraries over a state grid, emitted in the NuclearDataOneEnergy spline form.
  5. VERIFICATION: k-eff on one geometry by three routes — CE Monte Carlo, run_keff_mg on the collapsed library, genfoam diffusion on the bridged constants. Agreement within statistics is the test; disagreement localises to the step that caused it.

WHY IT MATTERS. Pebble bed: double heterogeneity means constants must be generated on TRISO-in-pebble-in-bed geometry, not a homogenised smear — pebble_beds::delta_tracking is the CE side. MSR: outram-park-fork-moltres IS a multigroup diffusion code with precursor drift and needs a salt library re-collapsed as salt temperature and density move.

NOT IN SCOPE: new transport physics; everything composes what exists. No V&V claimed — step 5 is the verification and until it passes a collapsed library is a number, not a validated one.

Related: op-375p / gh:#41 (neutronics API scope), op-jyyp (HTR-10 simulator).

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: CORRECTION: this bead says 'no MGXS tallies'. Wrong — the tally module already has Flux/Total/Fission/Absorption/NuFission/KappaFission/ScatterN plus Energy/Cell/Material/Universe/Mesh filters and a RegularMesh. Real gaps: no scatter MATRIX (ScatterN is (n,xn) scalar), RegularMesh is the only mesh so constants cannot land on an FvMesh, and the collapse/bridge. Step-by-step for both binning paths: op-c1dw / gh:#46.

title: MGXS extraction: MC tallies -> collapsed group constants -> genfoam

description:
Source: docs/melcor-parity-scoping.md (written 2026-08-07; banner-marked UNTRUSTED AI-ASSISTED DRAFT, human review pending).

Build a clean-room, lumped-parameter severe-accident capability from the PUBLIC MELCOR manuals (SAND2017-0876 / ML17040A420 and companions) plus legitimately-licensed component codes -- CFAST (NIST, public domain) for the executive and volume/vent architecture, AeroSolved/PartMC (GPL) for aerosols, FLEXPART (GPL-3.0) for dispersion.

WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT FROM EVERY OTHER PORT HERE: there is no open upstream. MELCOR, ASTEC and MAAP are all closed, and MELCOR specifically is distributed under a signed NDA that binds PEOPLE, not just artefacts. So this must be a clean-room reimplementation from public documents, assembled at COMPONENT level.

TARGET FOR THIS EPIC = "MELCOR-lite": a physically meaningful containment pressure, temperature and hydrogen history for a station-blackout-class LWR transient, with NO source term (no aerosols, no FP transport, no MCCI). Centres on a new NON-MESH lumped-parameter crate; touches outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs (flash kernel), tampines-steam-tables + outram-park-fork-coolprop (EOS), tuas_boussinesq_solver (conduction/convection), teh-o-prke (decay heat), outram-park-fork-offbeat (Zr oxidation), kovan-literature (manual ingest).

DONE = a runnable transient producing a citable containment P/T/H2 history, restartable, with plot-file output, and V&V documented (methodology AND measured results per the workspace rule) against public benchmarks -- QUENCH for oxidation, THAI HD/HM for hydrogen distribution, ISP-42/PANDA for containment mixing.

HARD CONSTRAINTS: intended use is education/research/V&V only -- never licensing, never PSA of a real facility, never emergency response. No MELCOR/ASTEC/MAAP/RELAP5/BISON/Griffin/SAM source may be touched or paraphrased by anyone, INCLUDING FROM MEMORY UNDER NDA. Every model must cite the public document it was written from, with ADAMS/SAND identifier, in its doc comment.

SCOPE ESTIMATES (self-labelled judgement in the source doc, +/- half their own value): MELCOR-lite ~70-105 kLOC; full parity ~200-320 kLOC. The COR full phase is explicitly marked as having NO honest schedule estimate.

DELIBERATELY NOT FILED as children of this epic, per the doc's own flags:
- MCCI / CAV: recommended DEFERRED. Blocked on closed CALPHAD databases (TAF-ID is signatory-only, NUCLEA restricted). The doc says explicitly: do not plan around acquiring them. This REVERSES docs/melcor-scoping.md:80,166, which called the thermochimica/corium extension "the highest leverage-per-effort item in the whole list".
- "Transcribe ANS-5.1": it is a purchased ANS standard. The doc flags the sourcing route as a MAINTAINER DECISION (open secondary source vs computing decay power from open ENDF decay data), not a recommendation.
- Phase 0 crate creation is a DECISION, not a task -- a new workspace member is not currently sanctioned anywhere in CLAUDE.md.
- containmentFOAM and OpenCalphad ports: their LICENSE files were NOT read. containmentFOAM's GPL-3.0-or-later is INFERRED from its OpenFOAM base; OpenCalphad's GPL version is not stated in its README. Read both before actioning any port issue.
Also note: the doc's test counts are static #[test] attribute counts, not passing counts -- only ~10 crates were actually run.
title: MELCOR-lite: clean-room lumped severe-accident code from public manuals

description: Scaffold + drive the reactor-multiphysics pipeline that reproduces Figure 4.29 (maximum fuel temperature during a control-rod-removal transient) of Xin Wang's 2018 UC Berkeley PhD dissertation 'Coupled neutronics and thermal-hydraulics modeling for pebble-bed FHR' (escholarship.org/uc/item/40q3985m). Wang used Serpent (MC) + COMSOL (SP3 via user-defined PDEs); the OUTRAM PARK re-implementation maps that onto njoy (MGXS) -> outram-mc/OpenMC (mesh+tally) -> GeN-Foam SP3 multiphysics (outram-foam-appbuilder-lib). Target case: Mk1 PB-FHR, 236 MW(th), 8 energy groups, flibe coolant, TRISO fuel pebbles; transient = remove 3 of 8 B4C control rods (prompt) from a core pre-loaded to 3941 pcm excess reactivity, 100 s. Scaffold lives in crates/nee_soon/src/xin_wang_sp3_workflow/. Committed thesis extraction: docs/xin-wang-thesis/. This is a SCAFFOLD epic; the actual run is beaded work below.
title: [epic] Xin Wang SP3 njoy->openmc->genfoam workflow (reproduce Fig 4.29 Mk1 control-rod-removal transient)

acceptance_criteria: IHX duty split reproduced at the design point with the process side as a boundary condition; the first coupled load is an EXISTING dwsim-libs distillation column reboiler duty, not a new process model; op-1z3o.1 updated with the FCC-autothermal reasoning.
description:
REVISED 2026-08-13 on maintainer direction. GTHTR300C: 600 MWt at 950 degC, IHX between RPV and gas turbine system, 170 MW of IHX duty to process heat, balance to electricity.

FCC IS OUT OF SCOPE - settled, with a technical reason worth keeping: fluid catalytic cracking is AUTOTHERMAL. The regenerator coke burn both regenerates the catalyst and supplies the cracking endotherm, so there is no external heat demand for nuclear to displace. Do not model it.

WHAT TO COUPLE TO INSTEAD - the workspace already owns one half of this (verified 2026-08-13):
  - DISTILLATION COLUMNS ARE REAL AND SUBSTANTIAL: crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/columns/ is 11,355 lines across 15 modules - bubble_point, newton_raphson, sum_rates, tridiagonal, thermo_bridge, specs, profile, initial_estimates, solver, plus dynamic.rs (853 lines) and shortcut.rs landed 2026-08-12. Column reboiler duty is a genuine high-grade heat demand and is the natural first coupling target.
  - HYDROGEN IS NOT BUILT: the only 'hydrogen' hits in crates/ are NUCLEAR hydrogen (H-1 / ZrH thermal scattering in outram-mc), not process hydrogen. The steam-methane reformer exists only as bead op-1z3o.7 (Gibbs equilibrium block, Todo). Steam cracking (>850 degC, purely fired) and hydrogen production remain the real targets, but both are unbuilt.

So the deliverable is: an IHX component model, plus the secondary-side process load as a BOUNDARY CONDITION - and the first credible load to attach is the existing dwsim-libs column reboiler duty, not a from-scratch process. Full iodine-sulfur process chemistry stays out of scope.

Feeds op-1z3o.1 (refinery demonstration-scope DECISION): the FCC-autothermal reasoning above should inform it, and the columns are the asset that already exists.
title: HTGR Phase 6 (stretch): GTHTR300C IHX — couple to the EXISTING distillation columns and hydrogen, not FCC

description:
In crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/array_control_vol_and_fluid_component_collections/fluid_component_collection/super_collection_series_and_parallel_functions.rs, the fn calculate_pressure_change_using_guessed_branch_mass_flowrate (declared :1184) sets SimpleConvergency { eps: 1e-9, max_iter: 70 } (:1310), tries find_root_brent (:1315), falls through its Err arm with only a dbg!, tries find_root_regula_falsi (:1332), falls through that Err arm with only a dbg!, and then reaches:

    todo!("debugging: all root finding methods used not successful");   // :1347

This ABORTS THE PROCESS on ordinary non-convergence. With max_iter 70 and eps 1e-9 that is a routine runtime outcome for a hard parallel network, not a theoretical one. The crate already has a TuasLibError type in scope, so returning Err is available.

Call sites: 5 in this file (:870, :993, :1027, :1075, :1098) plus 4 on a same-named sibling in collection_series_and_parallel_functions.rs (:620, :724, :758, :806).

This is the only todo!() in the file. (The crate has ~100 crate-wide, but those are overwhelmingly in test/calibration modules, not the library dispatch path -- this one is notable precisely because it is in the hot path.)

Fix: change the signature to return Result<Pressure, TuasLibError> and propagate, or return the best-effort bracket with a diagnostic error.

Verified 2026-08-07 against the working tree.
title: tuas: parallel-branch flow solver panics via todo!() on non-convergence (:1347)

description:
The studio frame everything else plugs into. An eframe app (target-gated off Android per the windowing exemption, like mesh_studio/mc_studio) with: a list/picker of every visual component, a live-state control panel (sliders for temperature, flow, opening fraction, etc.) so a widget can be driven across its full range by hand, and a panel showing the widget's derived geometry inputs so it is obvious what drives what.

Follow the crate's existing example-app conventions (examples/ with required-features, app_scaffold/ for shared panels). Tracer state is APPLICATION-owned and advanced once per frame, then copied into the widget at build time -- widgets are rebuilt every repaint, so a train owned by a widget resets its phase each frame (crate CLAUDE.md).

Parent: the Widget Studio bead.
